estimand: rank of the estimated beta matrix
scale_behavior: rank is invariant to nonsingular factor rescaling
threshold: rank must be at least the number of priced factors
justification: the second pass cannot identify all risk prices if beta columns are linearly dependent

estimand: cross-sectional standard deviation of beta_i_rate times standard_deviation(rate innovation)
scale_behavior: invariant to rescaling of the rate factor
threshold: at least 10 percent of the cross-sectional standard deviation of beta_i_mkt times standard_deviation(market factor)
justification: compares dispersion in fitted-return units instead of raw beta units
failure_interpretation: the short-rate column has too little economically scaled cross-sectional variation

estimand: standard deviation of the rate-factor residual after projection on other factors
scale_behavior: uses factor return units and is unaffected by beta normalization
threshold: residual standard deviation must exceed 10 percent of the raw rate-factor standard deviation
justification: a factor that is almost spanned by other factors has limited independent identifying variation
failure_interpretation: the rate factor is redundant with the comparator factor set

estimand: change in the rate-attributable fitted-premium spread after omitting each anomaly family
scale_behavior: uses fitted premium beta_i_rate times lambda_rate so it is factor-scale invariant
threshold: no sign reversal and no loss of materiality classification
justification: prevents one anomaly family from driving the economic conclusion
failure_interpretation: the pricing interpretation is fragile to test-asset composition

estimand: maximum influence of any portfolio on lambda_rate and pi_rate
scale_behavior: computed on fitted premiums and standardized parameter changes
threshold: absolute standardized influence must be below 1 for confirmatory interpretation
justification: guards against a single portfolio determining the rate price
failure_interpretation: the result is influential and must be reported as descriptive

estimand: joint-bootstrap confidence interval for pi_rate and equivalence statistics
scale_behavior: uses fitted-return units and recomputes beta and lambda jointly
threshold: interval must not span both economically positive and economically negative fitted-premium effects
justification: weak precision can make a significant risk price uninterpretable
failure_interpretation: the sign and economic magnitude of fitted premium are too imprecise

scale_behavior: parameter scale changes with factor normalization but interpretation is reported through fitted premium
threshold: no standalone confirmatory threshold; reported with fitted-premium bootstrap
justification: the article benchmark uses Shanken uncertainty for risk prices
failure_interpretation: asymptotic uncertainty is descriptive unless aligned with fitted-premium inference
